newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil says may reduce Statfjord output.
newsitem.headline: Statoil says may reduce Statfjord output.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Friday offshore crude loadings in the North Sea were suspended due to bad weather and it may be forced to reduce production at the Statfjord complex "soon" due to full storage tanks.
"There are high winds and waves and we had to stop loading yesterday," a spokeswoman for the company said.
"At Statfjord the tanks are 90 percent full and we will have to begin reducing (output) soon.

Statfjord pumps about 380,000 barrel per day (bpd) and processes crude from the Statfjord East and North satellites and the nearby Snorre and Vigdis developments, which in total add roughly 400,000 bpd to the Statfjord stream.
The spokeswoman could not provide the status of operations at Gullfaks, which produces around 475,000 bpd and handles around 85,000 bpd of output from the Tordis field.
Statoil said there were two vessel at Gullfaks ready to load when the weather improved, and one at Statfjord.
"They think it may be tomorrow," the spokeswoman said.
